sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye divase 'tha caturdaśe sametya rājakartāro bharataṃ vākyam abruvan
english: Then, at the break of dawn on the fourteenth day, the ministers of state assembled and addressed Bharata with these words.

sanskrit: gato daśarathaḥ svargaṃ yo no gurutaro guruḥ rāmaṃ pravrājya vai jyeṣṭhaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: "Daśaratha, who was the most revered of our elders, has gone to heaven — he who sent away Rāma, the eldest, and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa into exile."

sanskrit: tvam adya bhava no rājā rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ saṃgatyā nāparādhnoti rājyam etad anāyakam
english: "O prince of great glory, be our king today. Through circumstance alone this kingdom fails — for a realm without a ruler is no trifling matter."

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ sarvam idam ādāya rāghava pratīkṣate tvāṃ svajanaḥ śreṇayaś ca nṛpātmaja
english: "O Rāghava, O son of a king, your kinsmen and all the guilds await you, with all the requisites for royal consecration at hand."

sanskrit: rājyaṃ gṛhāṇa bharata pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat abhiṣecaya cātmānaṃ pāhi cāsmān nararṣabha
english: "Accept, O Bharata, this great kingdom inherited from your father and grandfathers. Consecrate yourself and protect us, O bull among men."

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ kṛtvā sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇam bharatas taṃ janaṃ sarvaṃ pratyuvāca dhṛtavrataḥ
english: Having circumambulated in reverence all the vessels and materials for the consecration rite, Bharata, firm in his vows, addressed the entire assembly with this reply.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhasya rājatā nityam ucitā hi kulasya naḥ naivaṃ bhavanto māṃ vaktum arhanti kuśalā janāḥ
english: "Kingship for our lineage properly belongs always to the eldest. Wise men such as you ought not to speak to me in this manner."

sanskrit: rāmaḥ pūrvo hi no bhrātā bhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ ahaṃ tv araṇye vatsyāmi varṣāṇi nava pañca ca
english: "Rāma, our elder brother, shall be lord of the earth. I shall dwell in the forest for fourteen years."

sanskrit: yujyatāṃ mahatī senā caturaṅgamahābalā ānayiṣyāmy ahaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ rāghavaṃ vanāt
english: "Let a great army of four divisions be made ready. I shall bring back my elder brother, Rāghava, from the forest."

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ caiva sarvam etad upaskṛtam puraskṛtya gamiṣyāmi rāmahetor vanaṃ prati
english: "Taking all these consecration materials arrayed before me and placing them at the fore, I shall set out toward the forest for Rāma's sake."

sanskrit: tatraiva taṃ naravyāghram abhiṣicya puraskṛtam āneṣyāmi tu vai rāmaṃ havyavāham ivādhvarāt
english: "Having consecrated that tiger among men there itself and honored him, I shall bring Rāma back — as fire is brought from a sacrifice."

sanskrit: na sakāmā kariṣyāmi svam imāṃ mātṛgandhinīm vane vatsyāmy ahaṃ durge rāmo rājā bhaviṣyati
english: "I shall not fulfill the desires of this woman who still smells of her mother's milk. I shall dwell in the difficult forest; Rāma shall be king."

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ śilpibhiḥ panthāḥ samāni viṣamāṇi ca rakṣiṇaś cānusaṃyāntu pathi durgavicārakāḥ
english: "Let craftsmen level the road — smoothing rough places; let scouts who know difficult terrain march ahead and follow along the path."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇaṃ taṃ rāmahetor nṛpātmajam pratyuvāca janaḥ sarvaḥ śrīmadvākyam anuttamam
english: As the prince spoke thus for Rāma's sake, the entire assembly replied with words that were auspicious and utterly excellent.

sanskrit: evaṃ te bhāṣamāṇasya padmā śrīr upatiṣṭhatām yas tvaṃ jyeṣṭhe nṛpasute pṛthivīṃ dātum icchasi
english: "May Śrī, the lotus-born goddess of prosperity, attend upon you who speak thus — you who desire to give the earth to your elder, the king's son."

sanskrit: anuttamaṃ tad vacanaṃ nṛpātmaja prabhāṣitaṃ saṃśravaṇe niśamya ca praharṣajās taṃ prati bāṣpabindavo nipetur āryānananetrasaṃbhavāḥ
english: "Those words you have spoken, O son of a king, are most excellent." Hearing them resound in their ears, tears of joy fell upon him — drops born from the eyes and faces of noble men.

sanskrit: ūcus te vacanam idaṃ niśamya hṛṣṭāḥ sāmātyāḥ sapariṣado viyātaśokāḥ panthānaṃ naravarabhaktimāñ janaś ca vyādiṣṭas tava vacanāc ca śilpivargaḥ
english: Having heard his words, the ministers, the full assembly, and those whose grief had departed spoke these words with joy; and the people devoted to that foremost of men, as well as the companies of craftsmen, were set in motion by his command.

sanskrit: atha bhūmipradeśajñāḥ sūtrakarmaviśāradāḥ svakarmābhiratāḥ śūrāḥ khanakā yantrakās tathā
english: Then those skilled in surveying the land, expert in the craft of laying lines, diligent in their own work, brave — the diggers and the operators of machines —

sanskrit: karmāntikāḥ sthapatayaḥ puruṣā yantrakovidāḥ tathā vardhakayaś caiva mārgiṇo vṛkṣatakṣakāḥ
english: — the work-overseers and master builders, men skilled in mechanical devices, carpenters, road-layers, and tree-cutters —

sanskrit: kūpakārāḥ sudhākārā vaṃśakarmakṛtas tathā samarthā ye ca draṣṭāraḥ puratas te pratasthire
english: — well-diggers, plasterers, and bamboo-workers, along with all capable overseers — these set out in the vanguard.

sanskrit: sa tu harṣāt tam uddeśaṃ janaugho vipulaḥ prayān aśobhata mahāvegaḥ sāgarasyeva parvaṇi
english: That vast flood of people, marching toward that destination with joy, shone brilliantly with great momentum, like the ocean at the full moon.

sanskrit: te svavāraṃ samāsthāya vartmakarmāṇi kovidāḥ karaṇair vividhopetaiḥ purastāt saṃpratasthire
english: Those skilled in road-making, taking their respective turns and equipped with instruments of every kind, set out ahead in orderly procession.

sanskrit: latāvallīś ca gulmāṃś ca sthāṇūn aśmana eva ca janās te cakrire mārgaṃ chindanto vividhān drumān
english: Cutting through creepers, vines, thickets, stumps, rocks, and trees of every kind, those men cleared the road.

sanskrit: avṛkṣeṣu ca deśeṣu ke cid vṛkṣān aropayan ke cit kuṭhāraiṣ ṭaṅkaiś ca dātraiś chindan kva cit kva cit
english: In stretches devoid of trees some planted trees; others cut here and there with axes, picks, and sickles.

sanskrit: apare vīraṇastambān balino balavattarāḥ vidhamanti sma durgāṇi sthalāni ca tatas tataḥ
english: Others, mightier still, demolished the clumps of vīraṇa grass and cleared away difficult passages and rough ground in every direction.

sanskrit: apare 'pūrayan kūpān pāṃsubhiḥ śvabhram āyatam nimnabhāgāṃs tathā ke cit samāṃś cakruḥ samantataḥ
english: Others filled wells and long-sunken pits with earth; still others leveled the low-lying sections all around.

sanskrit: babandhur bandhanīyāṃś ca kṣodyān saṃcukṣudus tadā bibhidur bhedanīyāṃś ca tāṃs tān deśān narās tadā
english: Men then bound together what needed binding, crushed what needed crushing, and broke through what needed breaking, in each stretch of land.

sanskrit: acireṇaiva kālena parivāhān bahūdakān cakrur bahuvidhākārān sāgarapratimān bahūn udapānān bahuvidhān vedikā parimaṇḍitān
english: In no great span of time they constructed canals carrying abundant water, of many forms, resembling the ocean; and many wells of various kinds, adorned with surrounding parapets.

sanskrit: sasudhākuṭṭimatalaḥ prapuṣpitamahīruhaḥ mattodghuṣṭadvijagaṇaḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtaḥ
english: The road had a surface smoothed with plaster, great trees in full bloom, flocks of intoxicated birds uttering their calls, and was adorned with pennants.

sanskrit: candanodakasaṃsikto nānākusumabhūṣitaḥ bahv aśobhata senāyāḥ panthāḥ svargapathopamaḥ
english: Sprinkled with sandalwood-scented water and decorated with flowers of every kind, the army's road shone magnificently — like the path to heaven.

sanskrit: ājñāpyātha yathājñapti yuktās te 'dhikṛtā narāḥ ramaṇīyeṣu deśeṣu bahusvāduphaleṣu ca
english: Then, having received their orders, the appointed officers, each acting according to his assignment, in pleasant regions abounding with sweet fruits —

sanskrit: yo niveśas tv abhipreto bharatasya mahātmanaḥ bhūyas taṃ śobhayām āsur bhūṣābhir bhūṣaṇopamam
english: — beautified yet further, with every kind of ornament, the encampment that the high-souled Bharata had intended — that which was itself like an ornament.

sanskrit: nakṣatreṣu praśasteṣu muhūrteṣu ca tadvidaḥ niveśaṃ sthāpayām āsur bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Those who were versed in such matters established the encampment of the high-souled Bharata under auspicious lunar mansions and at auspicious moments.

sanskrit: bahupāṃsucayāś cāpi parikhāparivāritāḥ tatrendrakīlapratimāḥ pratolīvaraśobhitāḥ
english: With many mounds of earth, surrounded by moats, with gateposts resembling Indra's bolt, adorned with grand avenues —

sanskrit: prāsādamālāsaṃyuktāḥ saudhaprākārasaṃvṛtāḥ patākā śobhitāḥ sarve sunirmitamahāpathāḥ
english: — fitted with rows of palaces, enclosed by walls of mansions, beautified with banners, all furnished with well-laid grand highways —

sanskrit: visarpadbhir ivākāśe viṭaṅkāgravimānakaiḥ samucchritair niveśās te babhuḥ śakrapuropamāḥ
english: — with lofty pavilion-topped towers seeming to spread across the sky, those encampments, tall and majestic, resembled the city of Indra.

sanskrit: jāhnavīṃ tu samāsādya vividhadruma kānanām śītalāmalapānīyāṃ mahāmīnasamākulām
english: Having reached the Jāhnavī — the Gaṅgā — with her forests of diverse trees, her cool and pure waters, and her abundance of great fish —

sanskrit: sacandratārāgaṇamaṇḍitaṃ yathā nabhaḥkṣapāyām amalaṃ virājate narendramārgaḥ sa tathā vyarājata krameṇa ramyaḥ śubhaśilpinirmitaḥ
english: — as the sky at night shines immaculately, adorned with the moon and multitudes of stars, so in due time that road shone resplendent — delightful, fashioned by skilled craftsmen of good craft.

sanskrit: tato nāndīmukhīṃ rātriṃ bharataṃ sūtamāgadhāḥ tuṣṭuvur vāgviśeṣajñāḥ stavair maṅgalasaṃhitaiḥ
english: Then, on that night dedicated to joyous ceremony, bards and panegyrists skilled in the art of speech praised Bharata with hymns filled with auspicious words.

sanskrit: suvarṇakoṇābhihataḥ prāṇadad yāmadundubhiḥ dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca śataśo vādyāṃś coccāvacasvarān
english: The time-drum struck with golden mallets resounded to life; hundreds of conches were blown, along with instruments of high and low tones.

sanskrit: sa tūrya ghoṣaḥ sumahān divam āpūrayann iva bharataṃ śokasaṃtaptaṃ bhūyaḥ śokair arandhrayat
english: That very great noise of the instruments, as though filling the sky, pierced Bharata, already scorched by grief, with fresh grief yet again.

sanskrit: tato prabuddho bharatas taṃ ghoṣaṃ saṃnivartya ca nāhaṃ rājeti cāpy uktvā śatrughnam idam abravīt
english: Then Bharata, having awakened, caused that din to be stopped; and having declared, "I am not the king," he said this to Śatrughna:

sanskrit: paśya śatrughna kaikeyyā lokasyāpakṛtaṃ mahat visṛjya mayi duḥkhāni rājā daśaratho gataḥ
english: "Look, Śatrughna — the great harm that Kaikeyī has done to the world. Leaving all sorrows upon me, King Daśaratha has departed."

sanskrit: tasyaiṣā dharmarājasya dharmamūlā mahātmanaḥ paribhramati rājaśrīr naur ivākarṇikā jale
english: "The royal glory of that righteous king, that high-souled one — a glory rooted in dharma — now drifts about, like a rudderless ship on water."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bharataṃ prekṣya vilapantaṃ vicetanam kṛpaṇaṃ ruruduḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṃ yoṣitas tadā
english: Seeing Bharata lamenting thus, beside himself, pitiable, all the women then wept aloud.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin vilapati vasiṣṭho rājadharmavit sabhām ikṣvākunāthasya praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ
english: While he was lamenting thus, Vasiṣṭha, the illustrious one, learned in the dharma of kings, entered the assembly hall of the lord of the Ikṣvākus.

sanskrit: śāta kumbhamayīṃ ramyāṃ maṇiratnasamākulām sudharmām iva dharmātmā sagaṇaḥ pratyapadyata
english: The righteous-souled one, together with his attendants, entered that hall — beautiful, fashioned of gold, richly set with gems and jewels — as one enters the Sudharmā, the assembly of the gods.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanamayaṃ pīṭhaṃ parārdhyāstaraṇāvṛtam adhyāsta sarvavedajño dūtān anuśaśāsa ca
english: He, the knower of all the Vedas, took his seat upon a golden throne covered with the most precious of cushions, and then gave instructions to the messengers.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān yodhān amātyān gaṇaballabhān kṣipram ānayatāvyagrāḥ kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ hi naḥ
english: "Bring quickly, without delay, the brāhmaṇas, the kṣatriyas, the warriors, the ministers, and the heads of the guilds — for we have pressing business."

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdo mahān samudapadyata rathair aśvair gajaiś cāpi janānām upagacchatām
english: Then a great clamor arose as people came thronging with chariots, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: tato bharatam āyāntaṃ śatakratum ivāmarāḥ pratyanandan prakṛtayo yathā daśarathaṃ tathā
english: Then the subjects welcomed Bharata as he arrived, just as the immortals welcome Indra — even as they had once welcomed Daśaratha.

sanskrit: hrada iva timināgasaṃvṛtaḥ stimitajalo maṇiśaṅkhaśarkaraḥ daśarathasutaśobhitā sabhā sadaśaratheva babhau yathā purā
english: The assembly, graced by the son of Daśaratha, shone as it had in Daśaratha's own time of old — like a lake teeming with great fish and noble elephants, its waters still, strewn with gems, conches, and pebbles.
